docs.title: Audio-reactive authoring
docs.text:
quickthumb.audio.analyze_audio(path, cache_dir=None) analyzes a local audio source ahead of authoring. It returns a validated AudioAnalysis record with transient onset times and source-relative RMS amplitudes. Onsets identify sharp increases in loudness; they are not a musical beat grid or a tempo estimate.

Use an onset as an ordinary numeric TimingSpec.start. This avoids a dependency on soundtrack options when sampling, restoring JSON, or rendering in workers:

from quickthumb import AnimationSpec, ColorTrack, KeyframeSpec, TimingSpec
from quickthumb.audio import analyze_audio

analysis = analyze_audio("music.wav")
if analysis.onsets:
    motion = AnimationSpec.timeline(
        ColorTrack(keyframes=[
            KeyframeSpec(time=0, value="#102030"),
            KeyframeSpec(time=0.2, value="#42CEB7"),
        ]),
        timing=TimingSpec(start=analysis.onsets[0], duration=0.2),
        easing="linear",
    )

Attach motion to a layer's animation=. See the runnable examples/audio_onsets.py for a scene, analysis sidecar, canonical JSON and MP4 with the same source as its soundtrack. The numeric motion is also inspectable with inspect_motion() and uses each target's existing color-track support or declared fallback. HTML presentation does not play the soundtrack; GIF remains silent. Baked timing is not a claim of live audio synchronization in either format.

docs.title: Source clock and RMS
docs.text:
All times are seconds from the beginning of the first decoded audio stream. Analysis uses mono audio resampled to 8 kHz and contiguous 160-sample (20 ms) windows. rms[i] is the linear RMS amplitude of the window starting at i * 0.02; the final window may be shorter. Values are source amplitudes, not normalized per track. Silence has zero RMS and no onsets.

The versioned detector requires an RMS attack above 0.01 and twice both the previous window and the mean of the previous ten windows, with at least 100 ms between anchors. Reference transients are tested within one 20 ms window; gradual attacks and musical offbeats need not produce anchors. An onset index can be absent: check onsets before indexing.

Export gain, soundtrack looping/fade-out, narration and other mixed audio do not change this source analysis. Deck timing is slide-local: authors must translate a soundtrack onset into the intended slide's clock. Nothing automatically repeats or relocates anchors when export options change.

docs.title: Loudness-driven scale
docs.text:
AudioAnalysis.scale_track(min_scale=1.0, max_scale=1.15) returns an ordinary ScaleTrack. Attach it to AnimationSpec.timeline(); no soundtrack or analyzer is consulted while converting stored RMS into motion:

pulse = AnimationSpec.timeline(
    analysis.scale_track(min_scale=1.0, max_scale=1.4)
)

The helper divides each RMS amplitude by the loudest window in this analysis, then maps that ratio into the requested scale range. Silence maps to min_scale, the peak maps to max_scale, and an entirely silent analysis stays at min_scale. This is source-relative normalization: a quiet recording can produce the same response as a louder copy, and export volume does not affect it. Both bounds must be finite positive numbers with max_scale >= min_scale.

Each keyframe holds its value over its 20 ms window, including a shorter final window; there is no interpolation before an attack. At the exact source end an additional keyframe returns to min_scale, so settled holds and subsequent slides do not retain a loud final pulse. The inferred animation duration equals analysis.duration. An explicit TimingSpec must allow that full duration; setting start shifts the entire source clock rather than trimming it.

The generated track is regular canonical JSON: sample(), inspect_motion(), workers and exporters consume it through the existing scale-track path. Reduced motion suppresses this track and keeps the authored static geometry. HTML/PPTX follow their declared scale support, but do not acquire live soundtrack playback or synchronization. The runnable example combines an onset-triggered color change and a loudness-driven scale pulse with source audio in MP4.

docs.title: Store and reuse
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path
from quickthumb.audio import AudioAnalysis

Path("analysis.json").write_text(analysis.model_dump_json(), encoding="utf-8")
stored = AudioAnalysis.model_validate_json(Path("analysis.json").read_text())

The record includes its schema/algorithm version, source SHA-256, FFmpeg version, sampling parameters, duration, ordered onsets and RMS windows. Its JSON schema is available through AudioAnalysis.model_json_schema(). A sidecar and motion baked into document JSON can be loaded and sampled without the source audio or FFmpeg. Exporting audio still requires its source and the usual media tools.

analyze_audio itself requires FFmpeg (QUICKTHUMB_FFMPEG overrides the binary). It caches records under the system temporary directory's quickthumb-audio folder, or the supplied cache_dir, using source bytes, algorithm, fixed parameters and FFmpeg version as the identity. Cache writes are atomic. Changing source bytes or decoder/algorithm versions creates a new entry; a corrupt entry raises an error identifying the file to remove. Keep a sidecar to pin authoring results across decoder upgrades rather than relying on an evictable cache.

Inputs are bounded to 64 MiB and ten minutes of decoded audio. Analysis has a 60-second timeout. Missing/non-audio files, unsupported FFmpeg filters and exceeded limits fail with actionable errors; analysis is never silently truncated. These limits bound authoring work, not rendering duration.

docs.title: Background
docs.text: .background() adds a full-canvas background layer. Multiple background calls stack in render order; the first call is at the back.

docs.title: Signature
docs.text:
canvas.background(
    color=None,
    gradient=None,
    image=None,
    opacity=1.0,
    blend_mode=None,
    fit=None,
    effects=None,
)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description color str \| tuple \| None None Solid fill color. Hex string ("#RRGGBB" or "#RRGGBBAA") or RGB/RGBA tuple. gradient LinearGradient \| RadialGradient \| None None Gradient fill. See Enums & Gradients. image str \| None None Local file path or remote URL. opacity float 1.0 Layer opacity from 0.0 (transparent) to 1.0 (opaque). blend_mode str \| BlendMode \| None None How this layer composites over previous layers. See BlendMode. fit str \| FitMode \| None None How an image fills the canvas. See FitMode. effects list \| None [] Background effects. Accepts Filter and Grain.

docs.title: Solid color
docs.text: canvas.background(color="#0F172A")

docs.title: Gradient overlay
docs.text:
from quickthumb import LinearGradient

canvas.background(
    gradient=LinearGradient(
        angle=120,
        stops=[("#111827", 0.0), ("#11182700", 1.0)],
    ),
    opacity=0.7,
)

docs.title: Remote image with effects
docs.text:
from quickthumb import Filter

canvas.background(
    image="https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1516321318423-f06f85e504b3",
    fit="cover",
    blend_mode="multiply",
    effects=[Filter(blur=4, brightness=0.75, contrast=1.1, saturation=0.9)],
)

docs.title: Dark overlay
docs.text: canvas.background(color="#000000", opacity=0.4)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Background layers always cover the entire canvas.
  • color, gradient, and image can each be used independently or together within one layer.
  • blend_mode applies when compositing this layer over previous layers.
  • Supports both local file paths and remote URLs for image.
  • For available effects, see Filter and Grain.

docs.title: Canvas
docs.text: The Canvas is the root object. It holds dimensions and an ordered list of layers. Its authoring fields follow the shared layer vocabulary, which also applies to Deck slides and canonical JSON.

docs.title: Canvas(width=None, height=None)
docs.text:
from quickthumb import Canvas

canvas = Canvas(1280, 720)
Parameter Type Description width int \| None Canvas width in pixels. Must be a positive integer. height int \| None Canvas height in pixels. Must be a positive integer.

Width and height must be given together or both omitted. A canvas built without a size (Canvas()) is unsized: it accepts layer builders but cannot be rendered, diagnosed, or serialized until it gets a size, either directly or by being added to a sized Deck, which gives it the deck's default size. Check canvas.has_size to tell the difference.

docs.title: Canvas.from_aspect_ratio(ratio, base_width)
docs.text:
Creates a canvas from an aspect ratio string and a base width. Height is calculated automatically.

wide     = Canvas.from_aspect_ratio("16:9", base_width=1280)   # 1280×720
square   = Canvas.from_aspect_ratio("1:1",  base_width=1080)   # 1080×1080
vertical = Canvas.from_aspect_ratio("9:16", base_width=1080)   # 1080×1920
Parameter Type Description ratio str Aspect ratio string in "W:H" format, e.g. "16:9" base_width int Canvas width in pixels

docs.title: Layer builders
docs.text:
All builder methods mutate the canvas and return self, enabling method chaining.

Method Description .background(...) Add a full-canvas background layer .text(...) Add a text layer .image(...) Add an overlay image layer .shape(...) Add a shape layer .svg(...) Add an SVG layer, rasterized at render time .group(...) Add an auto-layout group of child layers .outline(...) Add a canvas border .chart(...) Add a deterministic bar or line chart layer from a typed chart spec .qr_code(...) Add a square QR code layer .custom(fn) Add a Pillow callback layer

See the data visualization reference and the other individual reference pages for full parameter details.

docs.title: .diagnose()
docs.text:
Checks the composition for layout and legibility issues without writing a file. Returns a DiagnosticReport whose findings list contains Diagnostic entries (empty when clean):

for finding in canvas.diagnose().findings:
    print(finding.severity, finding.code, finding.message)

Finding codes: off-canvas, tiny-text, text-overflow, text-clipped, missing-glyph, low-contrast, layer-overlap, layer-hidden, and edge-crowding. See Diagnostics & CLI for details and the quickthumb lint (or quickthumb diagnose) equivalent.

docs.title: .prefetch_assets() (optional)
docs.text:
You never need to call this: render() and export() download remote images, SVGs, text fills, and fonts themselves, and export() returns the resulting asset_manifest. Call it only to do those downloads up front, to catch a network failure or a stale cache entry before a long export, or to warm the cache for later offline renders. It returns the manifest without rendering:

manifest = canvas.prefetch_assets().asset_manifest
if any(entry.status == "stale" for entry in manifest):
    ...  # decide whether to proceed with cached bytes

See Remote assets and caching for statuses, QUICKTHUMB_ASSET_MAX_AGE, and offline mode.

docs.title: .export(path, policy=None, *, format=None, quality=None, animation=None)
docs.text:
Writes the canvas like render() and returns an ExportResult whose written_paths lists the single written file. The path may be a string or pathlib.Path; format, quality, animation, and policy mean the same as in render().

result = canvas.export("card.png")
print(result.written_paths)

See Recommended output API for the result fields, the capability preflight, and how export() relates to the methods below.

docs.title: .render(path, format=None, quality=None, debug=False, animation=None, policy=None)
docs.text:
Renders the canvas and writes the result to a file. The format is detected from the file extension; .svg, .pptx, and .pdf produce vector/document output, and .gif/.mp4/.webm/.mov produce an animation playing the canvas's layer animation effects (see Exporting to SVG, PPTX, PDF & video). Canvas .lot output writes the bounded native-vector subset described in Lottie vectors, using LottieOptions for fps and final hold. Unsupported content is rejected before writing, without PNG fallback.

from quickthumb import GifOptions, VideoOptions

canvas.render("output.png")
canvas.render("output.jpg", format="JPEG", quality=85)
canvas.render("output.webp", format="WEBP", quality=90)
canvas.render("debug.png", debug=True)  # raster output with public layer-id bboxes
canvas.render("output.svg")
canvas.render("output.pptx")  # requires quickthumb[pptx]
canvas.render("output.pdf")   # requires quickthumb[pdf]
canvas.render("output.gif")   # animated; .mp4/.webm/.mov require the ffmpeg binary
canvas.render(
    "preview.gif",
    animation=GifOptions(fps=8, max_size=(540, 960), colors=128),
)
canvas.render("preview.mp4", animation=VideoOptions(fps=30))
Parameter Type Default Description path str — Output file path format str \| None None Case-insensitive raster encoding override: "PNG", "JPEG", or "WEBP"; rejected with document/animated extensions. quality int \| None None Compression quality: JPEG 1–95, WebP 1–100; other targets reject it. debug bool False Draw public layer-id bounding boxes on raster output for visual review. animation GifOptions \| VideoOptions \| LottieOptions \| None None Format-specific options: GifOptions for GIF, VideoOptions for MP4/WebM/MOV, LottieOptions for .lot. policy ExportPolicy \| None None Renderer policy, such as reduced_motion for animated, HTML, and PPTX output. Both render() and export() enforce unsupported_motion before writing. export() reports an explicitly requested static SVG fidelity check.

Warning

Passing quality with format="PNG" raises RenderingError. Passing debug=True for document or animated output (.svg, .pptx, .pdf, .html, .gif, .mp4, .webm, .mov, or .lot) raises RenderingError.

GifOptions, VideoOptions and LottieOptions are available from quickthumb. GifOptions accepts fps, hold, matte, loop, max_size=(width, height), and colors. VideoOptions accepts fps, hold, matte, soundtrack=AudioTrack(...), and loop_audio. VideoOptions(transparent=True) preserves alpha in VP9 WebM or ProRes 4444 MOV (strict boolean, default False); all other output targets reject this option. Both use a strict finite nonnegative hold (default 3 seconds), omitted from serialized options when equal to its default. Both accept workers (a strict integer from 1 to 8, default 1) and render_quality="standard" or "high" for rendering. See parallel animated rendering for spawn setup and supported inputs. GIF sizing and palette controls are rejected for MP4/WebM/MOV output.

docs.title: .to_svg(embed_fonts=False)
docs.text:
Returns the canvas as an SVG document string. Set embed_fonts=True to inline the used font files as @font-face data URLs.

svg = canvas.to_svg(embed_fonts=True)

docs.title: .to_pptx()
docs.text:
Returns the canvas as PowerPoint file bytes: a single slide with editable text boxes and autoshapes. Requires the pptx extra.

with open("deck.pptx", "wb") as f:
    f.write(canvas.to_pptx())

docs.title: .to_pdf()
docs.text:
Returns the canvas as PDF file bytes: a single page with native vector backgrounds, shapes, and selectable text when its font can be safely embedded and the text does not require complex shaping. Unsupported text is embedded as a pixel-exact image fragment. Requires the pdf extra.

with open("card.pdf", "wb") as f:
    f.write(canvas.to_pdf())

docs.title: .to_gif(...) / .to_mp4(...) / .to_webm(...) / .to_mov(...)
docs.text:
Return the canvas as an animation that plays its layer animation effects in sequence, then holds the settled composition for hold seconds (see Animated GIF & video). A canvas with no animations yields a single-frame GIF. .to_mp4()/.to_webm()/.to_mov() require the ffmpeg binary on PATH (or named by QUICKTHUMB_FFMPEG).

gif_bytes = canvas.to_gif(fps=20, hold=3.0, loop=0, matte="#000000")
mp4_bytes = canvas.to_mp4(fps=30, hold=2.0, soundtrack="music.mp3")
webm_bytes = canvas.to_webm(fps=30, hold=2.0)
overlay_bytes = canvas.to_webm(fps=30, hold=2.0, transparent=True)

.to_mp4()/.to_webm()/.to_mov() also accept soundtrack (an audio file muxed into the video, trimmed to the video length) and loop_audio (an explicit override). AudioTrack(..., loop=True) repeats a shorter configured track; legacy string paths keep the previous default of looping. GIF cannot carry audio. See the Deck API for the full parameter table.

All animated byte methods accept keyword-only workers=1 and render_quality="standard" ("high" enables supersampling). .to_gif() also accepts max_size=None for proportional resizing and colors=None for the palette size (2–256 when supplied). Existing positional parameters remain unchanged.

The keyword-only transparent flag on .to_webm() and .to_mov() skips only the export matte; authored backgrounds stay visible. See transparent WebM for codec, alpha decoding and transition details.

.to_mov() uses the same parameters and timing as .to_webm(), with fixed ProRes 4444 video and AAC audio. It retains odd and one-pixel dimensions. The RGBA source remains 8-bit; 16-bit alpha coding can decode with one-level 8-bit alpha differences, and color is lossy 4:4:4 YUV. See ProRes MOV for the measured conversion limits and encoder requirements. render() and export() accept .mov with VideoOptions for both opaque and transparent output.

docs.title: .export_image_sequence(output_directory, *, format="png", quality=None, matte=None, lossless=None, options=None, policy=None)
docs.text: Write the animated timeline as independent PNG (default), JPEG or WebP files plus manifest.json into a new directory under an existing parent. ImageSequenceOptions(fps=30, hold=3, workers=1, render_quality="standard") controls timing/compositing; method keywords select image encoding. JPEG uses RGB on an opaque matte (white by default), with quality=1..95. WebP preserves alpha and accepts lossless=True; lossy WebP accepts quality. PNG and lossless WebP preserve the renderer's exact RGBA8 pixels. Opaque WebP files may decode as RGB; manifest mode describes logical RGBA decoding. The receipt reports actual frame count, timing, encoding and destination. See image sequences for validation, per-format metadata and atomic no-overwrite publication.

docs.title: .to_base64(format="PNG", quality=None)
docs.text:
Returns the rendered image as a base64-encoded string.

b64 = canvas.to_base64(format="PNG")
b64 = canvas.to_base64(format="WEBP", quality=90)
Parameter Type Default Description format str "PNG" Output format: "PNG", "JPEG", or "WEBP" quality int \| None None Compression quality: JPEG 1–95 or WebP 1–100.

docs.title: .to_data_url(format="PNG", quality=None)
docs.text:
Returns the rendered image as a data URL (data:<mime>;base64,...).

url = canvas.to_data_url(format="JPEG", quality=90)
# → "data:image/jpeg;base64,..."
Parameter Type Default Description format str "PNG" Output format: "PNG", "JPEG", or "WEBP" quality int \| None None Compression quality: JPEG 1–95 or WebP 1–100.

docs.title: .inspect()
docs.text:
Returns a deterministic CanvasInspection containing layer identities, order, visibility, bounding boxes and authored text-layout metadata. No output file is written. Existing font/image assets may be read for sizing, but parent-layer drawing is not invoked.

report = canvas.inspect()
for layer in report.layers:
    print(layer.id, layer.bbox)

For supported parent-linked scenes, bounds describe the authored-static world layout, not the state at animation time zero. They conservatively enclose each existing measured local body after its ancestor transforms and can extend outside the canvas. Transparent corners can make these boxes looser than painted pixels. Text sizes/wrapping remain authored-local; intrinsic counters use their settled formatted text for these measurements, without sampling the timeline. Nulls have no visible body or bbox. canvas.render("debug.png", debug=True) overlays the same authored-static boxes. diagnose() uses the same authored-static world layout, with transformed painted alpha for overlap/occlusion and transformed glyph/background pixels for contrast. Parent opacity is not inherited. Geometry animation on an ancestor prevents a static footprint from being reported as permanently hiding another layer. Repair suggestions describe parent-local positions or containing group layout; world coordinates must not be copied directly into those local fields. A top-level group's own clip/mask restricts its complete painted source, including sampled counters in settled group slots. Inspection reports the boundary-intersected group box and keeps conservative laid-out child boxes. Each layer or group box intersects only its own finite boundary before applying world transforms; enclosing group boundaries do not cut descendant inspection boxes. Static leaves and nested structural groups can have their own clips and masks at several depths, using the top-level group's shared parent-local plane and original canvas dimensions for percentages. Inverted masks retain conservative boxes around their cutouts. Child transforms still use the full authored group body; the boundary does not clip independently linked children. Counter observations use settled text, including glyph backgrounds and preceding group content. Groups with descendant boundaries support plain, odometer and flip text counters in settled layout slots. Each counter's fragments are combined before its own boundary, and each nested group's children before that group's boundary; changing counter paint does not move siblings, pivots or independently linked children. Other intrinsic dynamic sources and authored stagger on any structural descendant remain guarded. The participating top-level group's own animation may override other authored descendant animations; an external ancestor's animation or only an inner group's animation does not qualify. Static inspection and diagnostics retain the authored layout and composition; HTML, SVG, PDF and PPTX retain whole-scene authored-static fallback for overridden descendant motion. Intrinsic counter clocks continue through that override; counter-group stagger remains guarded. Static graph-leaf groups with their own or descendant clip/mask boundaries can use root stagger through the existing partial horizontal-band adapter; it does not establish which child owns a band. See parent adapter boundaries.

docs.title: .to_json()
docs.text:
Serializes the canvas to a JSON string.

json_str = canvas.to_json()

Raises ValidationError if the canvas contains .custom(fn) layers (callbacks cannot be serialized).

docs.title: Canvas.from_json(json_str)
docs.text:
Deserializes a canvas from a JSON string.

canvas = Canvas.from_json(json_str)

Note

from_json() expects a JSON string, not a Python dict. Use json.dumps(data) first if you have a dict.

docs.title: .custom(fn)
docs.text:
Adds a callback that receives and returns a Pillow Image.

from PIL import ImageDraw
from quickthumb import Canvas

def draw_badge(image):
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(image)
    d.polygon([(70, 70), (240, 70), (155, 180)], fill="#FF3B30")
    return image

canvas = Canvas(512, 512).custom(draw_badge)
Rule Detail fn must be callable Receives a PIL.Image.Image Return value May return the same image (mutated), a new image of the same size, or None Errors Exceptions from the callback are wrapped as RenderingError Serialization Custom layers are not JSON-serializable

docs.title: Data visualizations
docs.text:
quickthumb includes a compact, deterministic chart layer and a QR code layer for dashboards, cards, and generated social graphics. Bar and line charts share ChartData, while each chart type has a focused style model; they are intentionally not a general-purpose plotting system.

from quickthumb import (
    BarChartSpec,
    BarChartStyle,
    Canvas,
    LineChartSpec,
    LineChartStyle,
)

canvas = (
    Canvas(800, 400)
    .chart(
        spec=BarChartSpec(
            data=[-4, 8, 12, 6],
            style=BarChartStyle(color="#2563EB", negative_color="#DC2626"),
        ),
        position=(40, 40),
        width=220,
        height=120,
    )
    .chart(
        spec=LineChartSpec(
            data=[2, 5, 3, 7],
            style=LineChartStyle(color="#7C3AED", fill="#DDD6FE"),
        ),
        position=(40, 200),
        width=440,
        height=120,
    )
    .qr_code("https://example.com", position=(620, 40), size=140)
)

docs.title: Shared chart data and style
docs.text:
ChartData(values=[...]) is useful when a generated spec wants a named data object; builders and JSON also accept a plain numeric list. Empty, constant, and negative series are valid. Values must be finite numbers, so NaN, infinity, and non-numeric values raise ValidationError.

BarChartStyle accepts color, padding, opacity, negative_color, and bar_gap. LineChartStyle accepts color, padding, opacity, fill, fill_opacity, stroke_width, point_radius, and show_points. Passing an option that has no meaning for the selected chart type raises ValidationError instead of silently changing nothing. The selected spec is passed to the single .chart() builder.

Line chart values are scaled to the plot box. Constant series sit on the vertical midpoint. Bar charts always include zero in their range, so positive and negative values render on opposite sides of the baseline. Empty series render no pixels.

docs.title: Layer builders
docs.text:
Builder JSON type Purpose .chart(spec, position, width, height) chart / bar Vertical bars with a zero-aware baseline when given BarChartSpec .chart(spec, position, width, height) chart / line Line chart with point markers by default when given LineChartSpec .qr_code(data, position, size) qr_code Square QR code with explicit error correction and quiet zone

In JSON, a chart layer stores its discriminated chart specification under "spec" (for example, { "type": "bar", "data": [1, -2] }).

The chart builder accepts pixel or percentage positions, align, opacity, and the existing clip and mask composition primitives. Chart layers can also be used as group children; the group assigns their positions automatically. QR codes accept foreground, background, error_correction (L, M, Q, or H), and quiet_zone. QR rendering raises RenderingError when the requested square is too small to preserve the generated QR module matrix. Charts and QR codes also accept the existing layer-level animation contract for PPTX and GIF/video exports; omitting it keeps the deterministic static behavior.

Chart and QR layers serialize through Canvas.to_json(), validate through Canvas.from_json(), and appear in quickthumb schema. SVG, HTML, PDF, and PPTX exports preserve them through the standard pixel-exact raster fallback.

docs.title: Deck
docs.text: A Deck is an ordered collection of Canvas slides. Each slide renders exactly as it would on its own; the deck adds multi-output export on top of the same pipeline. Slides retain the Canvas layer vocabulary and scene-local identities.

docs.title: Deck(width=None, height=None, slides=None, theme=None)
docs.text:
from quickthumb import Canvas, Deck

deck = Deck()                          # empty, no default size
deck = Deck(1280, 720)                 # default slide size for unsized slides
deck = Deck(slides=[cover, body])      # from pre-built canvases
Parameter Type Description width int \| None Default slide width. Provide with height or omit both. height int \| None Default slide height. slides list[Canvas] \| None Initial slides, in order. Each must be a Canvas. theme dict \| None Token groups shared with every slide's $theme.* references (slide-level themes win). Preserved across to_json()/from_json().

docs.title: Deck.from_aspect_ratio(ratio, base_width)
docs.text:
Creates a deck whose default slide size comes from an aspect ratio string, mirroring Canvas.from_aspect_ratio.

deck = Deck.from_aspect_ratio("16:9", 1280)   # default 1280×720

docs.title: Adding slides
docs.text:
Pass initial slides to the constructor (Deck(slides=[...])) and/or append them one at a time with .slide(canvas, transition=None, *, audio=None, duration=None, notes=None), which mutates the deck and returns self for chaining. When the deck has a default size, an unsized Canvas() inherits it; a canvas built with an explicit size keeps its own (and triggers a mixed-slide-size warning when it differs).

Method Description .slide(canvas, transition=None, *, audio=None, duration=None, notes=None) Append one Canvas; optional audio/duration configure narration, and notes appear only in HTML presenter mode 
deck = (
    Deck(1280, 720)
    .slide(
        Canvas().background(color="#101820").text(content="Cover", size=96, color="#FFFFFF"),
        audio="voice.wav",
        duration=2.5,
        notes="Introduce the central thesis.",
    )
    .slide(Canvas().background(color="#1A1A2E").text(content="Body", size=64, color="#FFFFFF"))
)

Adding an unsized canvas to a deck with no default size raises ValidationError: give the deck a size or size the canvas.

A deck is also a sequence: len(deck), deck[i], and iteration over slides all work. deck.slides and deck.notes return copies of the aligned slide and speaker-note lists, so mutating either returned list does not change the deck.

docs.title: .export(path, policy=None, *, format=None, quality=None, animation=None)
docs.text:
Writes the deck like render() and returns an ExportResult whose written_paths lists numbered slide files for raster output, or one PDF, PPTX, HTML, or animation file. The path may be a string or pathlib.Path; format, quality, animation, and policy mean the same as in render().

result = deck.export("slides.png")
print(result.written_paths)

See Recommended output API for the result fields, the capability preflight, and how export() relates to the methods below.

docs.title: .render(path, format=None, quality=None, animation=None, policy=None)
docs.text:
Renders the deck, dispatching on the output extension. Returns the list of written file paths.

from quickthumb import GifOptions, VideoOptions

deck.render("deck.pdf")      # one multi-page PDF (a page per slide)
deck.render("deck.pptx")     # one multi-slide PPTX (a slide per slide)
deck.render("deck.gif")      # one animation playing transitions between slides
deck.render(
    "preview.gif",
    animation=GifOptions(fps=8, max_size=(540, 960), colors=128),
)
deck.render("deck.html")     # one self-contained HTML slideshow
deck.render("slides.png")    # slides_01.png, slides_02.png, …
deck.render("slides.jpg", quality=85)
Extension Behavior .pdf Single multi-page PDF. Requires the pdf extra. .pptx Single multi-slide PPTX. Requires the pptx extra. .gif / .webm / .mov Single animation playing layer animations and slide transitions with default settings. WebM and MOV require ffmpeg (MOV uses prores_ks). .mp4 Animated timeline with optional per-slide narration; H.264/yuv420p video and AAC audio. Requires ffmpeg (and ffprobe for narration). For still slides, use static canvases and Cut() transitions. .html / .htm Single self-contained, animated HTML slideshow. .png / .jpg / .jpeg / .webp One file per slide as a zero-padded numbered sequence. Parameter Type Default Description path str — Output path; raster names become <stem>_NN<ext> format str \| None None Case-insensitive raster encoding override ("PNG", "JPEG", "WEBP"); rejected with document/animated extensions. quality int \| None None Compression quality: JPEG 1–95, WebP 1–100; other targets reject it. animation GifOptions \| VideoOptions \| None None Format-specific options: GifOptions for GIF, VideoOptions for MP4/WebM/MOV. policy ExportPolicy \| None None Renderer policy, such as reduced_motion for animated, HTML, and PPTX output. Both render() and export() enforce unsupported_motion before writing.

Warning

Passing quality with .pdf, .pptx, or animated output raises RenderingError, as does rendering an empty deck.

GifOptions and VideoOptions are available from quickthumb. GifOptions controls GIF frame rate, hold, loop count, matte, proportional max_size, and palette colors; VideoOptions controls MP4/WebM/MOV frame rate, hold, matte, soundtrack, and audio looping. Supply its soundtrack as AudioTrack(path="music.mp3", loop=True). VideoOptions(transparent=True) preserves alpha in VP9 WebM or ProRes 4444 MOV (strict boolean, default False); all other output targets reject this option. Both use a strict finite nonnegative hold (default 3 seconds), omitted from serialized options when equal to its default. Both accept workers (a strict integer from 1 to 8, default 1) and render_quality="standard" or "high" for rendering. See parallel animated rendering for spawn setup and supported inputs. Format-specific options are rejected when used with the other animated format.

docs.title: .to_html()
docs.text:
Returns a self-contained slideshow document. The normal audience view supports click, Space, and arrow-key navigation. Opening the document from quickthumb serve with the ?presenter query adds the current/next dashboard, speaker notes, a pause/resume/reset timer, and synchronized audience controls.

html = deck.to_html()
deck.render("slides.html")

Use quickthumb serve slides.py during development; Python sources expose the deck as a module-level deck, slides, or canvas variable.

docs.title: .to_pdf() / .to_pptx()
docs.text:
Return the deck as document bytes, one page/slide per canvas.

with open("deck.pdf", "wb") as f:
    f.write(deck.to_pdf())   # requires quickthumb[pdf]
pptx_bytes = deck.to_pptx()  # requires quickthumb[pptx]

docs.title: .to_gif(...) / .to_webm(...) / .to_mov(...)
docs.text:
Return the deck as an animation: each slide plays its layer animations, holds its settled state, and its transition animates the change into it (see Animated GIF & video for the timing model). .to_webm()/.to_mov() require the ffmpeg binary on PATH (or named by QUICKTHUMB_FFMPEG).

gif_bytes = deck.to_gif(fps=20, hold=3.0, loop=0, matte="#000000")
webm_bytes = deck.to_webm(fps=30, hold=3.0)
overlay_bytes = deck.to_webm(fps=30, hold=3.0, transparent=True)

All animated byte methods accept keyword-only workers=1 and render_quality="standard" ("high" enables supersampling). .to_gif() also accepts max_size=None for proportional resizing and colors=None for the palette size (2–256 when supplied). Existing positional parameters remain unchanged.

These controls also apply to .to_mp4(). Use static canvases and Cut() for still narrated slides. File options and byte methods both use hold. Animated video requires a positive default hold whenever a slide has neither narration nor an explicit duration; zero is still valid for Deck GIF and silent image sequences. Deck GIF ignores per-slide narration and explicit durations.

The keyword-only transparent flag on .to_webm() and .to_mov() skips only the export matte; authored backgrounds stay visible. See transparent WebM for codec, alpha decoding and transition details.

.to_mov() uses the same parameters and timing as .to_webm(), with fixed ProRes 4444 video and AAC audio. It retains odd and one-pixel dimensions. The RGBA source remains 8-bit; 16-bit alpha coding can decode with one-level 8-bit alpha differences, and color is lossy 4:4:4 YUV. See ProRes MOV for the measured conversion limits and encoder requirements. render() and export() accept .mov with VideoOptions for both opaque and transparent output.

docs.title: .export_image_sequence(output_directory, *, format="png", quality=None, matte=None, lossless=None, options=None, policy=None)
docs.text: Write the animated timeline as independent PNG (default), JPEG or WebP files plus manifest.json into a new directory under an existing parent. ImageSequenceOptions(fps=30, hold=3, workers=1, render_quality="standard") controls timing/compositing; method keywords select image encoding. JPEG uses RGB on an opaque matte (white by default), with quality=1..95. WebP preserves alpha and accepts lossless=True; lossy WebP accepts quality. PNG and lossless WebP preserve the renderer's exact RGBA8 pixels. Opaque WebP files may decode as RGB; manifest mode describes logical RGBA decoding. The receipt reports actual frame count, timing, encoding and destination. See image sequences for validation, per-format metadata and atomic no-overwrite publication.

docs.title: .to_mp4(...)
docs.text: Return the same animated timeline as .to_webm() in an H.264 MP4 container, including scheduled per-slide narration and an optional mixed soundtrack. Animated MP4/WebM/MOV export supports at most 64 narrated slides per Deck; silent slides do not count toward that operational FFmpeg input limit. For a file export, use deck.export("deck.mp4", animation=VideoOptions(soundtrack=AudioTrack(path="music.mp3", loop=True))). It mixes the background track with each slide's audio narration during rendering. Without explicit options, deck.export("deck.mp4") uses the same animated timeline with default VideoOptions().

docs.title: .diagnose()
docs.text:
Aggregates each slide's Canvas.diagnose() findings and adds deck-wide checks. Returns a DiagnosticReport whose findings list contains DeckDiagnostic entries:

for finding in deck.diagnose().findings:
    print(finding.slide_index, finding.code, finding.message)
Field Type Description code str Slide codes (off-canvas, tiny-text, …) or mixed-slide-size severity str "warning" or "error" message str Human-readable description slide_index int \| None Originating slide, or None for deck-wide findings layer_index int \| None Originating layer within the slide, when applicable layer_id str \| None Stable originating layer id, including group-child ids layer_name str \| None Originating layer name when present bbox dict \| None Measured canvas-space bounding box related_layers list[str] Layer ids involved in the finding measured dict Rule-specific measured values suggestion str \| None Repair hint when available

A mixed-slide-size warning is added when slides do not all share the same dimensions. The PDF path sizes each page to its slide, but PPTX export uses the first slide's size for the whole deck, so larger later slides are clipped by PowerPoint. Keep slides the same size when targeting .pptx.

docs.title: .prefetch_assets() (optional)
docs.text: Downloads every slide's remote assets up front and returns one deck-level asset_manifest, like Canvas.prefetch_assets(). Rendering and exporting fetch assets themselves, so call it only to surface network failures or stale cache entries before a long export.

docs.title: .to_json() / Deck.from_json(json_str)
docs.text:
Round-trips the deck through canonical JSON, reusing each canvas's serialization. The shape is {"kind": "deck", "width": ..., "height": ..., "theme": {...}, "slides": [<canvas spec>, ...]}, where every slide carries "kind": "canvas"; width/height (the default slide size) and theme are emitted only when set. JSON-authored slides may omit dimensions when the deck supplies a default size; canonical serialization materializes those inherited dimensions. Per-slide transition, audio, duration, and notes fields are preserved alongside the canvas fields. A top-level theme is shared with every slide so slides can use $theme.* tokens, exactly like Canvas.from_json.

spec = deck.to_json()
restored = Deck.from_json(spec)

Note

As with Canvas.to_json(), decks containing .custom(fn) slides cannot be serialized unless those callbacks are registered. from_json() expects a JSON string, not a dict.

docs.title: Effects
docs.text:
Effects change how a single layer is drawn. Each layer type accepts its own set, and passing one it doesn't accept raises ValidationError.

Effect Text Image, SVG, video Shape Background Stroke ✓ ✓ ✓ — Shadow ✓ ✓ ✓ — Glow ✓ ✓ ✓ — Filter — ✓ — ✓ Background ✓ — — — Grain — ✓ — ✓ Duotone — ✓ — — InnerShadow — ✓ ✓ — BackdropBlur — ✓ ✓ —

Pass effects as a list to the effects parameter of any layer:

from quickthumb import Shadow, Stroke

canvas.text(
    content="CLICK NOW",
    size=96,
    color="#FFFFFF",
    effects=[
        Stroke(width=4, color="#000000"),
        Shadow(offset_x=4, offset_y=4, color="#000000", blur_radius=8),
    ],
)

docs.title: Stroke
docs.text:
Draws an outline around text glyphs, image edges, or shape edges.

from quickthumb import Stroke

Stroke(width=4, color="#000000")
Parameter Type Description width int Stroke thickness in pixels. Positive integer. color str Stroke color. Hex string ("#RRGGBB" or "#RRGGBBAA").

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from quickthumb import Stroke, TextPart

canvas.text(
    content=[
        TextPart(text="BIG TEXT", color="#FFFFFF", effects=[Stroke(width=6, color="#000000")]),
    ],
    size=108,
    position=("8%", "50%"),
    align=("left", "middle"),
)

docs.title: Shadow
docs.text:
Adds a drop shadow offset from the layer.

from quickthumb import Shadow

Shadow(offset_x=4, offset_y=8, color="#000000", blur_radius=12)
Parameter Type Default Description offset_x int required Horizontal shadow offset in pixels. Can be negative. offset_y int required Vertical shadow offset in pixels. Can be negative. color str required Shadow color. Hex string. blur_radius int 0 Blur spread in pixels. Non-negative integer.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from quickthumb import Shadow

canvas.image(
    path="portrait.png",
    position=("74%", "54%"),
    width=420,
    height=520,
    effects=[Shadow(offset_x=0, offset_y=14, color="#000000", blur_radius=24)],
)

docs.title: Glow
docs.text:
Adds a soft colored halo around the layer.

from quickthumb import Glow

Glow(color="#B8FF00", radius=16, opacity=0.35)
Parameter Type Default Description color str required Glow color. Hex string. radius int required Glow spread radius in pixels. Positive integer. opacity float 1.0 Glow intensity from 0.0 to 1.0.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from quickthumb import Glow

canvas.text(
    content="ELECTRIC",
    size=96,
    color="#FFFFFF",
    effects=[Glow(color="#22d3ee", radius=24, opacity=0.5)],
)

docs.title: Filter
docs.text:
Applies image processing adjustments. Used on background layers and image layers.

from quickthumb import Filter

Filter(blur=4, brightness=0.75, contrast=1.1, saturation=0.9)
Parameter Type Default Description blur int 0 Gaussian blur radius. Non-negative integer. brightness float 1.0 Brightness multiplier. Positive float. 1.0 = no change, 0.5 = half brightness. contrast float 1.0 Contrast multiplier. Positive float. 1.0 = no change. saturation float 1.0 Saturation multiplier. Non-negative float. 0.0 = grayscale, 1.0 = no change.

All parameters default to neutral, so only set the ones you want to change.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from quickthumb import Filter

canvas.background(
    image="hero.jpg",
    fit="cover",
    effects=[Filter(blur=6, brightness=0.6, saturation=0.8)],
)

docs.title: Background (text fill)
docs.text:
Draws a filled rounded rectangle behind a text block. Only available on text layers.

from quickthumb import Background

Background(color="#111827CC", padding=(16, 24), border_radius=14, opacity=1.0)
Parameter Type Default Description color str required Fill color. Hex string ("#RRGGBB" or "#RRGGBBAA"). padding int \| tuple 0 Inner padding. int for uniform, (vertical, horizontal), or (top, right, bottom, left). border_radius int 0 Corner rounding in pixels. Non-negative integer. opacity float 1.0 Fill opacity from 0.0 to 1.0.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from quickthumb import Background

canvas.text(
    content="BREAKING NEWS",
    size=72,
    color="#FFFFFF",
    position=("8%", "50%"),
    align=("left", "middle"),
    effects=[
        Background(color="#CC0000", padding=(12, 20), border_radius=8),
    ],
)

Note

Background as an effect is separate from the .background() layer builder. The effect applies behind a text block; the layer covers the full canvas.

docs.title: Grain
docs.text:
Adds film-grain noise to a background or image layer.

from quickthumb import Grain

Grain(intensity=0.12, monochrome=True, blend_mode="overlay", opacity=1.0)
Parameter Type Default Description intensity float required Noise amplitude from 0.0 (none) to 1.0 (maximum). monochrome bool True True = luminance noise (grey grain); False = independent per-channel color noise. blend_mode str "overlay" How noise composites onto the layer. One of "overlay", "screen", "multiply", "normal". opacity float 1.0 Overall grain strength from 0.0 (invisible) to 1.0 (full). seed int \| None None RNG seed for deterministic output. None = random each render.

intensity=0.0 adds no noise.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from quickthumb import Canvas, Grain

canvas = (
    Canvas(1280, 720)
    .background(
        color="#1A1A2E",
        effects=[Grain(intensity=0.12, monochrome=True)],
    )
    .image(
        path="portrait.png",
        position=("70%", "50%"),
        width=400,
        height=500,
        align=("center", "middle"),
        effects=[Grain(intensity=0.08, monochrome=False, blend_mode="overlay", opacity=0.6)],
    )
)

Note

Grain works on background, image, SVG, and video layers, but not on text or shapes.

docs.title: Duotone
docs.text:
Maps the layer to two colors by brightness: dark areas take the shadows color and light areas the highlights color, with a smooth blend between. Useful for putting photos into brand colors.

from quickthumb import Duotone

Duotone(shadows="#0A1730", highlights="#7FADFF", opacity=1.0)
Parameter Type Default Description shadows str required Color for the darkest parts of the image. highlights str required Color for the lightest parts of the image. opacity float 1.0 How strongly the effect replaces the original colors, from 0.0 to 1.0.

docs.title: InnerShadow
docs.text:
A shadow drawn inside the layer's edges, which makes it look pressed in.

from quickthumb import InnerShadow

InnerShadow(offset_x=0, offset_y=6, color="#00000080", blur_radius=12)
Parameter Type Default Description color str required Shadow color; alpha in the color is respected. offset_x int 0 Horizontal offset in pixels. offset_y int 0 Vertical offset in pixels. blur_radius int 0 Blur radius in pixels. opacity float 1.0 Overall strength, from 0.0 to 1.0.

docs.title: BackdropBlur
docs.text:
Blurs whatever is already drawn behind the layer, within the layer's shape, like frosted glass. Combine it with a translucent fill so the layer still reads as a panel:

from quickthumb import BackdropBlur, Canvas

canvas = (
    Canvas(1280, 720)
    .background(image="photo.jpg", fit="cover")
    .shape(
        shape="rectangle",
        position=(80, 440),
        width=640,
        height=200,
        color="#FFFFFF33",
        border_radius=24,
        effects=[BackdropBlur(radius=24)],
    )
)
Parameter Type Default Description radius int required Blur radius in pixels. opacity float 1.0 How strongly the blurred backdrop shows, from 0.0 to 1.0.

docs.title: Align
docs.text:
Controls which point of a layer the position coordinate refers to, and the horizontal alignment of text.

from quickthumb import Align

docs.title: Values
docs.text: Enum String alias Horizontal Vertical Align.CENTER "center" center middle Align.LEFT "left" left middle Align.RIGHT "right" right middle Align.TOP_LEFT "top-left" left top Align.TOP_CENTER "top-center" center top Align.TOP_RIGHT "top-right" right top Align.BOTTOM_LEFT "bottom-left" left bottom Align.BOTTOM_CENTER "bottom-center" center bottom Align.BOTTOM_RIGHT "bottom-right" right bottom

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
# Enum value
canvas.image(..., align=Align.TOP_LEFT)

# String alias
canvas.image(..., align="center")

# (horizontal, vertical) tuple
canvas.image(..., align=("center", "middle"))

Horizontal tuple values: "left", "center", "right" Vertical tuple values: "top", "middle", "bottom"

docs.title: BlendMode
docs.text:
Controls how a layer composites over the layers drawn before it.

from quickthumb import BlendMode

docs.title: Values
docs.text: Enum String alias Effect BlendMode.NORMAL "normal" No blending; the layer is drawn on top BlendMode.MULTIPLY "multiply" Darkens by multiplying color values BlendMode.OVERLAY "overlay" Combines multiply and screen BlendMode.SCREEN "screen" Lightens by inverting, multiplying, and inverting again BlendMode.DARKEN "darken" Takes the darker of each pixel BlendMode.LIGHTEN "lighten" Takes the lighter of each pixel

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
# Enum value
canvas.background(image="texture.jpg", blend_mode=BlendMode.MULTIPLY)

# String alias
canvas.background(image="texture.jpg", blend_mode="multiply")

Available on: .background() and .image().

docs.title: FitMode
docs.text:
Controls how an image is scaled when a target size box is defined.

from quickthumb import FitMode

docs.title: Values
docs.text: Enum String alias Behavior FitMode.COVER "cover" Fill the box, cropping any overflow FitMode.CONTAIN "contain" Fit entirely inside the box; letterbox the rest FitMode.FILL "fill" Stretch to fill the box exactly (ignores aspect ratio)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
# Enum value
canvas.image(path="portrait.png", position=("75%", "55%"), width=420, height=520, fit=FitMode.COVER)

# String alias
canvas.image(path="portrait.png", position=("75%", "55%"), width=420, height=520, fit="cover")

Available on: .background(image=...) and .image(). Only applies when both width and height define a target box (or for background layers, the full canvas).

docs.title: LinearGradient
docs.text:
A linear color gradient defined by an angle and color stops.

from quickthumb import LinearGradient

LinearGradient(
    angle=135,
    stops=[("#FF5733", 0.0), ("#3333FF", 1.0)],
)
Parameter Type Description angle float Gradient direction in degrees. 0 = top to bottom, 90 = left to right. stops list[tuple[str, float]] List of (color, position) tuples. Position is a float from 0.0 to 1.0.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Top-to-bottom dark fade
LinearGradient(angle=0, stops=[("#000000", 0.0), ("#00000000", 1.0)])

# Diagonal blue-to-purple
LinearGradient(angle=135, stops=[("#3B82F6", 0.0), ("#8B5CF6", 1.0)])

# Three-stop gradient
LinearGradient(
    angle=90,
    stops=[("#FF0000", 0.0), ("#00FF00", 0.5), ("#0000FF", 1.0)],
)

Pass to .background(gradient=...):

canvas.background(
    gradient=LinearGradient(angle=120, stops=[("#0F172A", 0.0), ("#0F172A00", 1.0)]),
    opacity=0.8,
)

docs.title: RadialGradient
docs.text:
A radial color gradient emanating from a center point.

from quickthumb import RadialGradient

RadialGradient(
    stops=[("#FF5733", 0.0), ("#3333FF", 1.0)],
    center=(0.5, 0.5),
)
Parameter Type Default Description stops list[tuple[str, float]] required List of (color, position) tuples. Position is a float from 0.0 to 1.0. center tuple[float, float] (0.5, 0.5) Center of the gradient as (x, y) fractions of the canvas size.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Vignette (dark edges, bright center)
RadialGradient(
    stops=[("#00000000", 0.0), ("#000000CC", 1.0)],
    center=(0.5, 0.5),
)

# Off-center spotlight
RadialGradient(
    stops=[("#FFFFFF33", 0.0), ("#FFFFFF00", 1.0)],
    center=(0.25, 0.3),
)

Pass to .background(gradient=...):

canvas.background(
    gradient=RadialGradient(
        stops=[("#22d3ee33", 0.0), ("#22d3ee00", 1.0)],
        center=(0.5, 0.5),
    ),
)

docs.title: TextFillImage
docs.text:
An image used as a fill for text glyphs. The image is scaled to the text bounding box and masked to the glyph shapes.

from quickthumb import TextFillImage

TextFillImage(
    path="fire_texture.jpg",
    fit="cover",
)
Parameter Type Default Description path str required Local file path or remote URL for the fill image. fit str \| FitMode "cover" How the image is scaled to the text bounding box. "cover", "contain", or "fill".

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
from quickthumb import Canvas, TextFillImage

# Local file
canvas.text(
    content="FIRE",
    size=140,
    fill=TextFillImage(path="assets/fire_texture.jpg", fit="cover"),
    position=("50%", "50%"),
    align="center",
)

# Remote URL
canvas.text(
    content="MARBLE",
    size=140,
    fill=TextFillImage(
        path="https://example.com/textures/marble.jpg",
        fit="cover",
    ),
    position=("50%", "50%"),
    align="center",
)

Pass TextFillImage to the fill parameter of .text() or TextPart. See Gradient and image fills for usage in context.

docs.title: description: Reference for quickthumb group layers: auto-layout rows and columns with gap, padding, item alignment, and nesting.
Group (Auto Layout)
docs.text: .group() adds an auto-layout container that measures its children and stacks them along a row or column, so you don't place each child by hand. Because the group recomputes positions from each child's natural size, the same spec keeps working when the headline gets longer or a badge is added. That also makes groups a good fit for LLM-generated layouts.

docs.title: Signature
docs.text:
canvas.group(
    children,
    direction="column",
    gap=0,
    padding=0,
    position=None,
    align=None,
    item_align="start",
)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description children list required Child layers in stacking order. Dicts or layer models of type text, image, shape, svg, chart, qr_code, or nested group. direction str "column" Main axis: "column" stacks top-to-bottom, "row" left-to-right. gap int 0 Pixels between adjacent children along the main axis. Non-negative. padding int \| tuple 0 Inner padding: a single int, (vertical, horizontal), or (top, right, bottom, left). position tuple \| None None Anchor point of the group box, in pixels or percentage strings. align str \| Align \| tuple \| None None Which point of the group box the position refers to, like image layers. See Align. item_align str "start" Cross-axis placement of each child: "start", "center", or "end".

Children must not set position

The group assigns positions. A child that sets its own position raises ValidationError, and a child's align is ignored; use item_align on the group instead.

canvas = Canvas(1280, 720).background(color="#16213E").group(

        {"type": "text", "content": "AUTO LAYOUT", "size": 96, "color": "#FFFFFF", "weight": 900},
        {"type": "text", "content": "No coordinates were harmed", "size": 40, "color": "#A2A8D3"},

)

docs.title: Nested groups
docs.text:
Groups can nest, so a column can contain a row (and vice versa):

canvas.group(
    children=[
        {"type": "text", "content": "RELEASE 0.5", "size": 96, "color": "#FFFFFF", "weight": 900},
        {
            "type": "group",
            "direction": "row",
            "gap": 14,
            "children": [chip("GROUPS"), chip("TOKENS"), chip("LINT")],
        },

    direction="column",
    gap=28,
    position=("7%", "50%"),
    align=("left", "middle"),

docs.title: Cross-axis alignment
docs.text:
canvas.group(
    children=[
        {"type": "text", "content": "CENTERED", "size": 80, "color": "#FFFFFF", "weight": 900},
        {"type": "text", "content": "Both children share a center line", "size": 36, "color": "#A2A8D3"},
    ],
    direction="column",
    gap=18,
    item_align="center",            # cross-axis: center each child horizontally
    position=("50%", "50%"),
    align=("center", "middle"),
)

docs.title: How sizing works
docs.text:
1. Each child is measured at its natural size (text bounds, image dimensions, shape width/height).
  2. Children are placed one after another along the main axis, separated by gap.
  3. The group box is the union of the children plus padding.
  4. The whole box is anchored to position according to align.

docs.title: JSON form
docs.text:
Groups serialize like any other layer. See the JSON Schema page for the full schema:

{
  "type": "group",
  "direction": "column",
  "gap": 24,
  "position": ["8%", "50%"],
  "align": ["left", "middle"],
  "item_align": "start",
  "children": [
    { "type": "text", "content": "AUTO LAYOUT", "size": 96, "color": "#FFFFFF", "weight": 900 }
  ]
}

docs.title: Validation rules
docs.text:
• children must be a non-empty list.
  • Children must not set position (the group assigns positions).
  • Valid child types: text, image, shape, svg, group.
  • gap cannot be negative; padding values cannot be negative, and a padding tuple must have 2 or 4 elements.

docs.title: Document inspection and sampling
docs.text:
Use inspect_document() when a tool or agent handles both Canvas and Deck documents. It combines the existing layout, motion, and diagnostic reports with the observed asset manifest in a DocumentInspection envelope:

from quickthumb import Canvas, Deck, inspect_document

document = Deck(slides=[Canvas(320, 180).background(color="#FFFFFF")])
report = inspect_document(document, target="video", fps=24, max_samples=100)
print(report.model_dump_json(indent=2))

for page_index, page in enumerate(report.pages):
    print(page_index, page.width, page.height, len(page.layers))

docs.title: Common fields
docs.text:
Field Meaning for either document kind version Result schema version, currently "1" kind Source document discriminator: "canvas" or "deck" width, height First page dimensions in pixels, matching the animated output stage pages One CanvasInspection for a Canvas, or every Deck slide in document order motion The existing MotionInspection, including timing, sampled property states, per-slide details, capability rows, and export diagnostics diagnostics The existing DiagnosticReport; Deck findings retain slide_index, including null for document-wide findings asset_manifest Observed asset references, resolution status, and available identity/hash/cache information

Every page retains layer identities, order, nested children, bounding boxes, and text measurements. Mixed-size Deck pages keep their own dimensions. The outer size is the first page's size, even when an authored Deck default differs; the existing deck.inspect() still reports that authored default.

target accepts one exporter family (raster, html, pptx, or video), an iterable of families, or None for all four. policy, fps, and max_samples are passed to inspect_motion() unchanged. Motion observations are bounded by max_samples; they are property states, not raster frames. Empty Decks and invalid options raise the existing structured Quickthumb errors.

The call writes no export. Like the individual inspection/diagnostic methods, it can load fonts, resolve assets, or decode media for measurement. The manifest describes the state after those operations; it does not initiate another prefetch or certify unresolved resources as available. Use prefetch_assets() when explicit resolution is wanted, and doctor for environment readiness.

canvas.inspect() and deck.inspect() keep their existing result types and JSON fields. Use those narrower methods when only layout is needed.

DocumentInspection.model_json_schema() describes this result envelope. The document-authoring schemas still describe input specs, not this result. As with DiagnosticReport, diagnostic findings deserialize as ordinary JSON objects; read their code, severity, message, and location fields rather than relying on a Python finding class after a JSON round trip.

docs.title: Join canonical samples to layout
docs.text:
Both document kinds already return the same FrameSequence from sample(). Its uniform sample grid is an observation clock, not an encoded frame index; see animation timing for GIF/video quantization and narration differences. Page indexes are zero-based and match frames[].slide and timeline[].slide:

from quickthumb import DocumentInspection, FrameSequence

layout = DocumentInspection.model_validate_json(report.model_dump_json())
samples = FrameSequence.model_validate_json(document.sample().model_dump_json())
for frame in samples.frames:
    page = layout.pages[frame.slide]
    print(frame.index, frame.time, frame.width, frame.height, len(page.layers))

No document-kind branch is needed for this loop. kind still identifies the source, and all per-page and per-frame details remain available.

  • sample() captures one authored-static RGBA frame per page with its own dimensions and transparency; time is None, duration is zero, and timeline is empty
  • sample(time=[0, 0.5]) or sample(fps=24) captures the animated timeline, with frames in time order, first-page stage dimensions, and an opaque matte
  • frames[].index orders the observations, while frames[].slide identifies the active page; the timeline segments describe page timing and transitions
  • environment records renderer versions; each frame carries its raw RGBA data and SHA-256 digest for deterministic comparisons in that environment

Timing has separate meanings: report.motion.duration retains the existing authored-motion inspection semantics. samples.duration is the canonical capture duration, including its hold argument and resolved narration timing. For example, a static Canvas has motion duration zero but a timed sample with hold=2 lasts two seconds. Use the sample's duration, fps, timeline, and frame time fields for playback comparisons; do not infer those from the layout report or motion property samples.

docs.title: Path
docs.text:
Canvas.path() draws filled or stroked SVG path data without an SVG file or an optional rendering dependency:

from quickthumb import Canvas

canvas = Canvas(160, 120).path(
    "M 0 0 H 100 V 100 H 0 Z M 25 25 H 75 V 75 H 25 Z",
    position=(20, 10), width=120, height=100,
    view_box=(0, 0, 100, 100), color="#42CEB7", id="frame",
)
canvas.export("path.png")
Parameter Meaning d SVG M/L/H/V/C/S/Q/T/A/Z commands, absolute or relative. Repeated coordinate sets, compact arc flags and implicit closing for fills are supported. position Required frame position in canvas pixels or percentages. width, height Required positive frame dimensions in pixels. view_box Optional (x, y, width, height) local coordinate window; defaults to (0, 0, width, height). Its width and height must be positive. color Flat fill color, default black; None disables flat fill. fill Existing LinearGradient or RadialGradient; when present it replaces color, including when color=None. stroke, stroke_width Optional solid stroke color and positive width in local units; width defaults to 1. line_cap "butt" (default), "round" or "square" for open endpoints. line_join "miter" (default), "bevel" or "round" for joined segments. miter_limit Maximum vertex-to-tip distance divided by half the stroke width; defaults to 4, must be at least 1. Longer miters become bevels. dash_array Optional tuple of nonnegative finite dash/gap lengths in local units. Odd-length tuples repeat once; empty or all-zero tuples draw a solid stroke. dash_offset Static distance into the repeated pattern, in local units; defaults to 0. Signed values wrap modulo the pattern cycle. id, motion_key Optional scene identity and cross-scene matching key, using the common layer identity rules. rotation, opacity, anchor, animation Static angle and opacity, normalized viewport pivot, and position/rotation/scale/opacity track timelines; see Path motion.

The local window maps independently onto the frame's width and height and is clipped at its edges. The frame does not fit itself to changing path bounds. Inspection reports that fixed frame. The fill uses the even-odd rule: an odd number of boundary crossings paints, so nested contours make holes regardless of their direction. Raster drawing supersamples only the visible painted bounds at 4× and downsamples with antialiasing.

C/S draw cubic Béziers and Q/T draw quadratic Béziers. Smooth commands reflect the preceding control point only within their own curve family, following SVG rules. Curves are adaptively flattened after mapping to the frame, with a 1/8-pixel chord tolerance before supersampling. Excessive plans raise RenderingError (path_subdivision_limit) instead of silently reducing precision; simplify the path or reduce its mapped scale.

A/a draw rotated elliptical arcs with SVG radius correction. Radii use their absolute values; a zero radius draws a line, and identical endpoints omit the arc. Large-arc and sweep flags must each be 0 or 1. Arc subdivision uses the same mapped chord tolerance and work limits. Unrepresentable numerical geometry raises RenderingError (path_arc_range_limit) rather than producing invalid pixels.

Strokes are centered on the path and scale with the viewBox, including independent horizontal and vertical scaling. Z joins the closing seam; returning to the start with a line leaves two capped endpoints. Stroke coverage is unioned before color is applied, so translucent intersections do not darken. Fill is painted first and stroke above it, both clipped to the fixed viewport. Round geometry uses the same 1/8-pixel chord tolerance. Excessive stroke geometry raises RenderingError (path_stroke_limit) before output is written.

canvas.path("M10 50C30 0 70 100 90 50", (20, 10), 120, 100, None,
            stroke="#42CEB7", stroke_width=8, line_cap="round",
            view_box=(0, 0, 100, 100), dash_array=(12, 6), dash_offset=3)

Dash phase restarts at each subpath. A dash crossing a corner keeps its join; painted runs meeting across a closed seam join there. Dash endpoints use line_cap, including zero-length on entries, and zero-length gaps advance to the next entry. Square dots follow the path tangent. Negative or nonfinite lengths, nonfinite offsets and overflowing cycle totals are rejected before admission. Patterns are limited to 65,536 entries; excessive transitions or emitted geometry raise RenderingError (path_dash_limit) before writing output. Use longer dash intervals or simplify the path.

Gradient coordinates use the fixed frame, matching shape fills: linear angle 0 runs left-to-right and 90 top-to-bottom; radial center is normalized to the frame. view_box maps the path geometry into that field. Paint bounds and canvas clipping crop the field without stretching or restarting it. Existing gradient stops support alpha, which is multiplied by the path's even-odd coverage before compositing. Stroke remains a separate solid color.

from quickthumb import LinearGradient

canvas.path("M10 10H90V90H10Z", (20, 10), 120, 100, None,
            view_box=(0, 0, 100, 100),
            fill=LinearGradient(angle=30, stops=[("#42CEB780", 0), ("#315D8EFF", 1)]))

Track timelines, static rotation/opacity and normalized anchor are supported; see Path motion for transform and source limits. Parent links, grouping and composition controls are not accepted yet. JSON uses type="path" and round-trips through PathLayer. The runnable path layer example combines Bézier curves, arcs, a gradient, stroke and an even-odd hole, then scales the viewport from 1× to 4× over two seconds. Its PNG is the authored still; the GIF plays the enlargement and the JSON preserves the complete source.

PNG and canonical samples draw the path at its sampled transform. Untransformed paths in SVG and HTML use native SVG with even-odd fill, fixed viewport clipping, gradients and local stroke controls. Transform timelines use a declared authored-static PNG fallback. Supported HTML stroke timelines use the native adapter described below. HTML keeps each slide's gradient resources independent.

Very large, tiny or poorly conditioned coordinates use a declared raster fallback when native numeric range or 1/8-pixel coordinate precision cannot be preserved. Gradient stops outside 0..1 also use raster output to retain their existing interpolation. validate_export() and ExportResult give the actual per-layer route and reason. ExportPolicy(unsupported_motion="error") permits native paths and rejects a required fallback before writing.

Untransformed PDF paths emit editable native curves, converting quadratics exactly and elliptical arcs to cubic curves bounded to 1/8 device pixel. It preserves even-odd clipping, local strokes and opaque frame gradients. Translucent gradient stops and paths exceeding the bounded cubic conversion use a declared raster fallback. Degenerate strokes and mixed zero-length dash patterns also use raster output to preserve cap pixels. Paths with static rotation/opacity or animation use the same authored-static PNG fallback in PDF as SVG/HTML. PPTX embeds an authored-static raster image.

docs.title: Animated dash phase
docs.text:
DashOffsetTrack (type="dash_offset" in JSON) animates stroke phase in local SVG/viewBox distance units. The sampled phase is added to authored dash_offset; negative offsets and odd-length dash patterns retain the static painter's cycle rules. Keyframes use the shared easing, outgoing holds, and local timeline clock. Tracks replace the relative phase by default; blend="add" composes additional phase tracks in event order. Only Path layers accept this track.

from quickthumb import AnimationSpec, DashOffsetTrack, KeyframeSpec, TimingSpec

phase = AnimationSpec.timeline(
    DashOffsetTrack(keyframes=[KeyframeSpec(time=0, value=0),
                               KeyframeSpec(time=1, value=12)]),
    timing=TimingSpec(duration=1), easing="linear",
)
canvas.path("M0 10H100", (10, 10), 100, 20, None,
            stroke="#42CEB7", dash_array=(5, 3), dash_offset=2, animation=phase)

Canonical samples, raster frames, GIF, video, and PNG sequences use the effective phase; inspect_motion() reports it alongside the authored static phase. SVG, PDF, and PPTX retain their declared authored-static fallback for animated Paths. HTML supports the bounded native stroke adapter described below. Path morphing uses the raster contract below.

docs.title: Stroke trim
docs.text:
trim_start and trim_end select normalized 0..1 positions along the total local SVG/viewBox arc length, in contour order. Move commands add no distance and never connect contours. The default 0, 1 retains the entire stroke, regardless of offset; equal endpoints and 1, 0 retain no stroke. When start exceeds end, the interval wraps across the end of the complete path.

trim_offset shifts both endpoints in normalized turns and wraps modulo one; negative and multiple-turn values are supported. A retained full closed contour keeps its closing join. A partial closed contour becomes open, with the authored caps at its cut endpoints; a wrapped selection through its closing seam keeps that seam as an interior join. Partial trims omit zero-length contours. Fill and gradient coverage remain authored and untrimmed. Dashes apply after trimming and restart with dash_offset at each retained run.

Lengths use the existing adaptive curve subdivision with a 1/8-device-pixel chord tolerance. The 65,536-point geometry budget still applies; unrepresentable length or cuts raise RenderingError (path_trim_limit) rather than emitting cap dots.

from quickthumb import TrimEndTrack

reveal = AnimationSpec.timeline(
    TrimEndTrack(keyframes=[KeyframeSpec(time=0, value=0),
                            KeyframeSpec(time=1, value=1)]),
    timing=TimingSpec(duration=1), easing="linear",
)
canvas.path("M0 10Q50 -10 100 10", (10, 10), 200, 40, None,
            view_box=(0, -10, 100, 20), stroke="#42CEB7", animation=reveal)

TrimStartTrack and TrimEndTrack replace their authored normalized boundaries. TrimOffsetTrack adds its sampled relative turns to authored trim_offset; its tracks replace that relative offset by default, with blend="add" for ordered composition. JSON types are trim_start, trim_end, and trim_offset. Only Path layers accept these tracks. Shared easing, outgoing holds, and local clocks apply; boundary easing stays within 0..1. Inspection reports effective trim values.

Canonical samples, GIF/video and PNG sequences use sampled trim geometry through the adaptive Path source. Static trims in SVG/PDF and all PPTX paths use a declared raster fallback. HTML supports the bounded native stroke adapter below; other animated document paths retain authored trim values. Path morphing is described below.

docs.title: Native HTML stroke motion
docs.text:
HTML can animate one canonical stroke-property timeline on a single nondegenerate contour using native SVG stroke-dasharray and stroke-dashoffset. Dash-offset motion preserves the authored local dash pattern, including odd patterns and negative phases. Fill and gradient paint use a separate, untrimmed SVG path.

Native trim requires an open contour with butt caps, no authored dash pattern, and an ordered, nonwrapping window throughout the animation. Trim start/end and relative offset tracks can combine within those bounds. Closed trim contours, wrapped windows, trim plus dash painting, transform tracks, lists of animation specs, and overshooting easing retain an explicit authored-static raster fallback. Static trim uses the same admission rules. PPTX keeps its static raster route.

The existing HTML runtime drives native stroke CSS keyframes sampled from the canonical timeline at 120 Hz, retaining every authored knot and outgoing hold boundary. Delays and triggers use the existing timeline clock. Between samples, CSS interpolates linearly; this is a bounded approximation of easing and curve length, rather than an exact browser/raster pixel guarantee. The plan permits at most 4097 stops (about 34 seconds without additional knots). Exceeding that plan uses the declared static fallback.

The generic HTML capability matrix reports partial support. Each admitted layer reports its actual native SVG/CSS route and sampled timing limit; rejected layers report the fallback reason. Strict export policy accepts admitted native routes and rejects combinations requiring raster fallback before writing output.

docs.title: Path morphing
docs.text:
PathMorphTrack (type="path_morph") accepts SVG d strings in ordinary KeyframeSpec values. It replaces path geometry in the fixed authored viewport; paint, trim, dash phase, opacity and transforms keep their existing semantics. The canonical sampler applies the shared local clock, per-segment easing and outgoing holds. Easing progress is clamped to 0..1. At authored keyframe boundaries it returns the original d string, retaining the original curves. Inspection exposes authored and effective geometry as path_morph.

from quickthumb import PathMorphTrack

change = AnimationSpec.timeline(
    PathMorphTrack(keyframes=[
        KeyframeSpec(time=0, value="M10 10H50V50H10Z"),
        KeyframeSpec(time=1, value="M20 20H60V60H20Z"),
    ]), timing=TimingSpec(duration=1), easing="linear",
)
canvas.path("M10 10H50V50H10Z", (10, 10), 100, 100, animation=change)

Correspondence uses the existing local SVG curve subdivision, then 256 equally spaced arc-length points per contour. Contours match in document order. Closed contours preserve winding and nesting; cyclic start alignment minimizes matched point distances, choosing the lowest shift when scores tie. Open contours retain authored direction and endpoints. Intermediate geometry is a polyline, with collinear interior points omitted, painted through the existing adaptive Path source and its single-entry cache.

This bounded subset requires 1–16 nondegenerate, noncrossing contours with matching count, order, open/closed status, winding and nesting. Touching or self-crossing contours are refused. A contour may use at most 256 locally subdivided vertices; the correspondence plan permits at most 4096 total sampled points and one million edge-pair checks. Resampling must retain each subdivided vertex within ¼ local SVG unit of its corresponding arc interval; otherwise admission fails. These local limits do not promise subpixel accuracy after enlargement. Endpoint geometry stays exact; intermediate contour positions interpolate linearly after easing.

Incompatible authored geometry raises ValidationError with code path_morph_topology. An intermediate sample that degenerates, intersects, touches, or changes winding/nesting raises RenderingError with that code before painting. The sampler does not silently reorder contours, reverse winding, crossfade, or substitute another topology. Endpoint geometry and correspondence plans use bounded caches; rendered frames still retain only the existing one-entry Path source.

Morph timelines render in canonical samples, GIF/video, and serial/worker PNG sequences. HTML, SVG, PDF and PPTX retain explicit authored-static raster fallback for this feature. The runnable path morph example uses one logo geometry twice: trim reveals its outline, OpacityTrack fades in its fill, then both layers morph together into a circle.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description shape str required Shape type: "rectangle", "ellipse", "pill", "triangle", "star", or "polygon". position tuple required (x, y) position. Values can be integers (px) or percentage strings ("50%"). width int required Shape width in pixels. Positive integer. height int required Shape height in pixels. Positive integer. color str required Fill color. Hex string ("#RRGGBB" or "#RRGGBBAA"). fill LinearGradient \| RadialGradient \| None None Gradient fill, painted through the shape and rotated with it. color stays the flat fallback for targets that cannot draw a gradient (PPTX, PDF, SVG, HTML). border_radius int 0 Corner rounding in pixels. Only applies to "rectangle". See Align. points list[tuple[float, float]] \| None None Vertices for "polygon" shapes, normalized 0.0–1.0 within the shape box. At least 3 points. star_points int 5 Number of star spikes. Only applies to "star". Minimum 3. inner_radius float 0.5 Inner-to-outer radius ratio for "star", strictly between 0.0 and 1.0. effects list \| None [] List of effects: Stroke, Shadow, Glow.

docs.title: Label rectangle
docs.text:
from quickthumb import Shadow, Stroke

docs.title: Gradient and image fills
docs.text:
Fill text glyphs with a gradient or image instead of a flat color. Pass a LinearGradient, RadialGradient, or TextFillImage to fill.

from quickthumb import Canvas, LinearGradient, RadialGradient, TextFillImage, TextPart

# Linear gradient headline
canvas.text(
    content="GRADIENT",
    size=120,
    fill=LinearGradient(angle=90, stops=[("#FF6B6B", 0.0), ("#4ECDC4", 1.0)]),
    position=("50%", "50%"),
    align="center",
)

# Image-filled text
canvas.text(
    content="TEXTURE",
    size=140,
    fill=TextFillImage(path="fire_texture.jpg", fit="cover"),
    position=("50%", "50%"),
    align="center",
)

# Per-segment fills using TextPart
canvas.text(
    content=[
        TextPart(
            text="HOT ",
            fill=LinearGradient(angle=45, stops=[("#FF4500", 0.0), ("#FFD700", 1.0)]),
            weight=900,
        ),
        TextPart(
            text="COLD",
            fill=LinearGradient(angle=45, stops=[("#00BFFF", 0.0), ("#8A2BE2", 1.0)]),
            weight=900,
        ),
    ],
    size=110,
    position=("50%", "50%"),
    align="center",
)

fill on a TextPart overrides the layer-level fill for that segment only. fill and color are independent; when fill is set it takes visual precedence. See TextFillImage for image fill options.
